q1_issues.issue: The antecedent is the opaque kind-level relation (Hunt sky_cat nightmoth), which no actual hunting event can ever produce, so the rule can never fire; the definite "that lantern-row" points at an episodic reading whose premise should be a hunt event pattern with sky-cat agent and nightmoth object.

q2_gaps: how a bare-plural clause sitting in an indicative conditional's ANTECEDENT is encoded — as the opaque kind-level relation of Striking & relational generics, or as an event pattern an episodic event can trigger; the conditional rule and the relational-generic rule are stated independently and their interaction is undefined

solid (single-word, unhyphenated) compounds such as "nightmoth": Compound concepts keys on symbols you fused from a multi-word surface form and says nothing about whether a genus is emitted for a compound already written as one word
notes: Hunt is licensed as a kind-level relation under Core patterns' opaque heads, LocatedIn is correct for "at", and the crowd's Member+GroupOf pair follows the "a flock of birds" collective-noun rule. Projecting the consequent's definite typing atoms at top level is right; the unmarked present on "thins" correctly takes no status atom.
